entry.title: Why Your HTTPS Traffic Still Gets Blocked (and How DPI Evasion Works)
entry.summary: You've set up your development environment, configured your proxy, everything is running over HTTPS — and your traffic still gets dropped. No error message, no timeout, just... nothing. If you've ever worked behind a restrictive corporate firewall or tried to reach package registries from a locked-down network, you know this pain. The culprit is usually Deep Packet Inspection (DPI), and understanding how it works will save you hours of debugging. Here's the thing most developers don't realize: even though HTTPS encrypts your payload, there's metadata leaking everywhere. The biggest offender is the SNI (Server Name Indication) field in the TLS handshake. entry.summary: New: One stream. Now it goes everywhere you need it. Dev, staging, and prod. Real-time processing and long-term storage. No duplicate pipelines, no config drift, and no extra cost.
